phases.label: The Solution
phases.description: DuPont markets GenX as 'Setting a New Industry Standard for Sustainable Replacement Technology.' Claims: 'favorable toxicological profile' and 'virtually complete elimination from the body in 12-24 hours.' Patents filed, EPA submissions made, production ramping at Fayetteville Works. Zero peer-reviewed scrutiny. Zero independent verification.

phases.label: First Signal
phases.description: A compound with zero prior literature suddenly appears in peer-reviewed journals. SENTINEL flags velocity-from-zero event.

phases.label: Public Discovery
phases.description: Star-News breaks the story. 300,000 people learn their water is contaminated. Lawsuits filed within months.

phases.label: Research Explosion
phases.description: Publication velocity doubles annually. Toxicity studies, environmental monitoring, regulatory attention accelerate.

phases.label: The Reckoning
phases.description: Billions in settlements. EPA drinking water regulation. Class certification for 100,000+ residents.

key_events.label: PFOA Stewardship Program
key_events.description: EPA launches voluntary program: 8 companies commit to eliminate PFOA by 2015. DuPont CEO pledges: 'We are developing potential alternative technologies.'

key_events.label: GenX PMN Filed with EPA
key_events.description: DuPont submits premanufacture notices for HFPO-DA and its ammonium salt under TSCA. Claims: 'favorable toxicological profile and very rapid bioelimination.'

key_events.label: EPA Consent Order
key_events.description: EPA enters TSCA consent order requiring DuPont to capture/destroy 99% of GenX compounds. DuPont begins customer conversions.

key_events.label: GenX Patent & Marketing Brochure
key_events.description: US Patent 7,662,324 issued (Feb 16). DuPont publishes 'GenX Processing Aid for Making Fluoropolymer Resins: Setting a New Industry Standard for Sustainable Replacement Technology' (Jul). Claims: 'favorable toxicological profile,' 'very rapid bioelimination,' 'virtually complete elimination from the body occurs in 12-24 hours in laboratory animals, compared with months for PFOA,' and 'unique environmental exposure control technologies.' DuPont tells NC DEQ GenX will replace PFOA at Fayetteville Works.

key_events.label: First Detection (Unpublished)
key_events.description: EPA researchers Strynar & Lindstrom detect GenX downstream of Fayetteville Works in the Cape Fear River. Results discussed at conferences but not yet published.

key_events.label: Found in Drinking Water
key_events.description: GenX sampled before and after water treatment — concentrations unchanged. Standard treatment cannot remove it. DuPont completes GenX transition from PFOA.

key_events.label: First Peer-Reviewed Papers
key_events.description: Strynar et al. publishes discovery of GenX and 11 other novel PFECAs in the Cape Fear River. Chemours spun off from DuPont. GenX detected in waterways in China and Germany.

key_events.label: Story Breaks / Lawsuits
key_events.description: Wilmington Star-News reports GenX in drinking water for 300,000 people (Jun 7). CFPUA announces lawsuit (Aug). NC DEQ sues Chemours (Sep 7). Federal grand jury subpoenas issued.

key_events.label: Consent Order
key_events.description: Chemours, NC DEQ, and Cape Fear River Watch sign remediation consent order. Thermal oxidizer installed Dec 31.

key_events.label: EPA IG Report
key_events.description: EPA Inspector General finds communication breakdown allowed GenX discharge for 8 years in violation of the 2009 consent order.

key_events.label: EPA Toxicity Assessment
key_events.description: EPA releases final human health toxicity assessment for HFPO-DA. NCDEQ settles with Chemours for $13M.

key_events.label: $2.2B Chemours Settlement
key_events.description: Chemours agrees to $2.2 billion environmental remediation settlement.

key_events.label: $10.3B 3M + Class Certification
key_events.description: 3M $10.3 billion PFAS public water settlement. Federal judge grants class certification for 100,000+ NC GenX residents.

key_events.label: EPA Drinking Water Rule
key_events.description: EPA announces final National Primary Drinking Water Regulation for HFPO-DA (GenX). The replacement chemical is now itself regulated.

industry_claims.source: DuPont PMN Submission to EPA (TSCA Section 5(a))
industry_claims.claim: Favorable toxicological profile and very rapid bioelimination.
industry_claims.reality: EPA's 2021 toxicity assessment found liver toxicity, kidney effects, developmental toxicity, and immune suppression at low doses.

industry_claims.claim: Virtually complete elimination from the body occurs in 12-24 hours in laboratory animals, compared with months for PFOA.
industry_claims.reality: While blood half-life is shorter, GenX persists in the environment indefinitely. Detected in drinking water, groundwater, rainwater, and soil across multiple continents.

industry_claims.claim: Setting a New Industry Standard for Sustainable Replacement Technology.
industry_claims.reality: EPA finalized National Primary Drinking Water Regulation for GenX (HFPO-DA) in 2024 — the 'sustainable replacement' is now itself a regulated contaminant.
EPA Inspector General found GenX discharged into the Cape Fear River for 8 years in violation of the 2009 consent order. 300,000 people drank contaminated water.

industry_claims.source: EPA TSCA Consent Order with DuPont
industry_claims.claim: DuPont required to capture and destroy 99% of GenX compounds during manufacturing.
industry_claims.reality: GenX detected in the Cape Fear River by 2012. By 2017, found in finished drinking water at levels unchanged by standard treatment.

sentinel_reconstruction.narrative: In 2010, DuPont published a brochure calling GenX a 'Sustainable Replacement Technology' with a 'favorable toxicological profile.' For the next five years, zero independent scientists examined this claim — zero peer-reviewed papers. SENTINEL would have flagged this silence: an actively manufactured chemical with industry safety claims and no independent verification. When the first papers appeared in 2015, SENTINEL would have escalated to NOVEL — a velocity-from-zero event on a compound already in production for six years. That was two years before the first lawsuit and seven years before the first billion-dollar settlement.
sentinel_reconstruction.counterfactual: With SENTINEL active in 2012, the detection of GenX in the Cape Fear River — even unpublished — would have triggered monitoring. By 2015, the first publications would have elevated the alert. A 2-year head start on litigation preparation could have changed the trajectory of a $14.5 billion exposure. More importantly, SENTINEL would have flagged the gap between DuPont's 2010 safety claims and the absence of any independent verification — a silence that lasted five years.
sentinel_reconstruction.key_insight: The most dangerous signal was not the hockey stick — it was the silence that preceded it. For eight years, a chemical was manufactured, marketed as safe, and discharged into a river that served 300,000 people. Zero peer-reviewed papers. Zero independent verification. DuPont's own brochure was the only 'evidence.' When the first paper finally appeared, the clock was already ticking.
